harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Enabled and persisted a ufw-based host firewall on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04): default policy rejects incoming, allows outgoing; explicit allow rules for tcp/22 (SSH) and tcp/8080; ufw service enabled at boot. Verified enforcement at the kernel nftables level and via live connection tests (8080 reachable with a bound listener, an unrelated port refused). Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id, issued a background systemctl reboot whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed a changed boot_id (fresh uptime), and re-verified ufw active/enabled with identical rules and nftables policy post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/firewall tooling and existing listeners (ufw present but inactive, only SSH listening)
Set ufw default incoming policy to reject and outgoing to allow
Added ufw allow rules for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp
Enabled ufw (--force enable) and confirmed it is systemd-enabled for boot persistence
Verified kernel-level nftables ruleset shows input chain policy drop with explicit accept for tcp dport 22 and 8080 (IPv4 and IPv6)
Ran a temporary test HTTP listener on 8080, confirmed reachability (HTTP 200) and confirmed an unrelated port (9999) was refused
Cleaned up the temporary test listener
Captured pre-restart boot_id and firewall/service state baseline on node1
Issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot on node1 so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned, confirming restart via changed boot_id and fresh uptime
Re-verified post-restart ufw active/enabled state and identical nftables enforcement rules

evidence.requirement: Firewall permits SSH and TCP 8080, rejects unrelated inbound (configuration applied)
evidence.summary: ufw configured with default reject incoming/allow outgoing plus explicit allow rules for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp, then enabled; status verbose shows active with those rules.

evidence.requirement: Firewall rules enforced at kernel level
evidence.summary: nft list ruleset shows input chain policy drop with explicit accept for tcp dport 22 and 8080 (IPv4 and IPv6).

evidence.requirement: Live proof that allowed port works and unrelated port is rejected
evidence.summary: Started a temporary listener on 8080; curl to $NODE_IP:8080 returned HTTP 200 while nc to an unrelated port 9999 was refused; listener then cleaned up.
systemctl is-enabled ufw returns 'enabled' both before rule application and after enabling the firewall.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 4d70780a-0bff-4d50-8c53-62faa1ccc945 and confirmed ufw active/enabled with correct rules prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2 && systemctl reboot' command returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: proof of changed boot identity
evidence.summary: First poll still showed old boot_id, second poll timed out during reboot, third poll returned new boot_id ea1bf088-870d-48c2-b297-1dffa22893a8, proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery of firewall state
evidence.summary: After reboot, uptime -s shows a fresh boot time (08:50:34, immediately after restart); ufw status verbose shows active/enabled with identical reject-incoming default and allow rules for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp; nft ruleset confirms identical policy drop input chain with accept rules for both ports.
